subject: giant walking dragline
title: A 13,000-Ton Machine Walked Across Ohio Without Wheels

scenes.text: A thirteen-thousand-ton machine walked across Ohio. It had no wheels.
Big Muskie stood twenty-two stories tall and dug coal for twenty-two years.
Each bite lifted three hundred twenty-five tons. A bulldozer could park in its bucket.
So how did it move? Two giant feet on its sides lifted it and slid it forward.
One slow step at a time, over a road of wooden beams so it wouldn't sink.
In 1999 it was scrapped. Only the bucket survives. The feet that walked are gone.

description:
A thirteen-thousand-ton machine once walked across Ohio, and it had no wheels.
Big Muskie, a Bucyrus-Erie 4250-W dragline, stood about 222 feet tall and scooped 325 tons per bite with a 220-cubic-yard bucket. It moved on two huge hydraulic walking feet over a prepared road of wooden beams.
It was scrapped in 1999; its bucket is preserved at Miners' Memorial Park in McConnelsville, Ohio.
Would you rather see it walk or see it dig?
first_comment: The bucket alone weighs 230 tons empty, and it still sits in an Ohio park today. What giant machine should we cover next?
